classification.difficultyReason: Four unsignposted diagram problems require selection and combination of supplementary/reflex, isosceles and parallel-line properties, including converting concave outside sectors and determining a nine-sided angle sum. The synthesis exceeds routine single-rule angle substitution; the givens constrain each chain.

spec.description: Triangle with both baseline extensions, exterior base angles and a reflex apex arc. Ordinary source blue linework is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Exterior base angles 119 degrees and 116 degrees; theta is the reflex apex angle.

answer.worked:
The interior base angles are supplementary to the given exterior angles.
$$\begin{align*}180^\circ-119^\circ&=61^\circ\\180^\circ-116^\circ&=64^\circ\\\text{Interior apex angle}&=180^\circ-61^\circ-64^\circ\\\text{Interior apex angle}&=55^\circ\\\theta&=360^\circ-55^\circ\\\theta&=305^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Three parallel horizontals and two extended transversals. Double ticks mark the top horizontal triangle side and its right oblique side; labels retain their source sectors.
spec.mathematics: Equal marked sides make the upper triangle isosceles. The 108-degree angle is below the bottom horizontal and left of the falling transversal; theta is above the bottom horizontal and left of the rising transversal.

answer.short:
$126^\circ$

Use the equal sides of the upper triangle, then the parallel lines.
answer.worked:
The upper triangle's right base angle is $180^\circ-108^\circ=72^\circ$, using corresponding angles and angles on a straight line. Its top angle and left base angle are equal because their opposite sides have matching ticks.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Left base angle}&=(180^\circ-72^\circ)\div2\\\text{Left base angle}&=54^\circ\\\theta&=180^\circ-54^\circ\\\theta&=126^\circ\end{align*}$$
The last step uses corresponding angles and angles on a straight line.

spec.description: Nine-sided concave boundary with two inward notches, all numerical angle labels, an upper-right right-angle square and the exterior reflex arc at the lower-left point.
spec.mathematics: Interior notch angles are 360-51 and 360-27 degrees. The lower-left interior angle is 360-311 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Derived interior angles and theta's value are absent.

answer.short:
$107^\circ$

Convert the marked outside angles to interior angles and use the polygon angle sum.
answer.worked:
The interior angles at the two notches are $309^\circ$ and $333^\circ$. The interior angle beside $311^\circ$ is $49^\circ$. Splitting a nine-sided polygon into seven triangles gives an interior-angle sum of $7\times180^\circ=1260^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=1260^\circ-(121^\circ+309^\circ+97^\circ+90^\circ\\&\qquad+76^\circ+49^\circ+333^\circ+78^\circ)\\\theta&=1260^\circ-1153^\circ\\\theta&=107^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Downward-pointing stepped figure with outer-side extensions, two parallel markers, 127-degree exterior angle, 88-degree step angle and reflex theta.
spec.mathematics: The right sloping side makes 53 degrees with a rightward horizontal. The upward step segment makes 88 degrees with that horizontal, leaving a 35-degree small bottom angle.

answer.worked:
Imagine a horizontal through the bottom vertex parallel to the marked lines. The right sloping ray makes $180^\circ-127^\circ=53^\circ$ with its rightward direction. The upward step ray makes $88^\circ$ with the same direction, using alternate angles.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Small bottom angle}&=88^\circ-53^\circ\\\text{Small bottom angle}&=35^\circ\\\theta&=360^\circ-35^\circ\\\theta&=325^\circ\end{align*}$$
